candidates.label: Pamphylia (label point)
candidates.support: Pamphylia's identity as the coastal plain of southern Asia Minor, with Lycia to the west and the mountains of Pisidia to the north, is undisputed. The label point is Pleiades' entry for the region. Because the region is small, the point falls about 9 km from this project's Perga pin.

summary.text: Pamphylia was a narrow, fertile coastal plain in southern Asia Minor. Paul and his company sailed from Paphos and 'came to Perga in Pamphylia,' and Paul's later voyage to Rome crossed 'the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia.' As described for Perga on this map, sources differ on which province held Pamphylia at about AD 50.

history.text: Sources differ on Pamphylia's province in about AD 50. The Roman historian Cassius Dio reports that in AD 43 Claudius incorporated the Lycians into the district of Pamphylia, but the Roman historian Tacitus records that under the Roman emperor Galba (AD 68-69) the provinces of Galatia and Pamphylia had a single governor, and other sources describe Pamphylia as part of Galatia until the Roman emperor Vespasian created the joint province of Lycia and Pamphylia after AD 70. Following the same reasoning as for Perga, this project treats Pamphylia as part of Galatia at about AD 50.

The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia notes a later change to Pamphylia's extent: in AD 70, after this project's about AD 50 date, the Romans added the Pisidian highlands to Pamphylia. Its article on Pisidia dates the transfer of southern Pisidia to the new province of Lycia and Pamphylia to AD 74.

scripture.textWEB: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
